item.text: {"text":"The closest architectural precedent is [MTAM (2020)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.08598): temporal gates modify recurrent state transitions and information filtering, with a time-aware GRU capturing short-term intent. Recent work supports distinguishing elapsed time from sequence order: [E-NSDE (NeurIPS 2024)](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/7cdbd53dfbcf9a5263227555aac5b9cd-Abstract-Conference.html) models continuously evolving preferences and interval-dependent uncertainty, although its differential-equation backbone is outside the required GRU family. [FAAM-SR (2026)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ins.2026.123580) introduces a frequency-adaptive GRU balancing repetitive and exploratory behavior; relevant evidence for adaptive gating, but not specifically timestamp-driven forgetting.\n\nA compatible experimental hypothesis—not an established result from these papers—is one jointly trained GRU whose reset/update gates receive log-transformed observed inter-event gaps. Alternatively, learn a bounded retention vector that attenuates the previous hidden state before the GRU update, allowing selective forgetting after long gaps. Compare ordinary GRU, gap-conditioned gates, and soft state attenuation under the fixed validation protocol. Use only timestamps already observed in each prefix; never require the unknown next interaction time. Skip padding updates and read the final nonpadding position of left-padded histories. Keep a single trained network and checkpoint per category; these sources do not establish that hard resets or temporal gating improve this particular Amazon benchmark."}
